description: The two extremes of the record's three fields, in ascending key order, seeded at the copybook's full 50 bytes so this case declares no normalisation. app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy fixes the geometry mechanically - XREF-CARD-NUM PIC X(16), XREF-CUST-ID PIC 9(09), XREF-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11), FILLER PIC X(14), which is 50 - and each row is that layout held at a limit. The first row is all zeros: XREF-CUST-ID and XREF-ACCT-ID at their minimum, and a card number of sixteen zero characters. The second is at the maximum every picture allows - 999999999 and 99999999999 - with a fourteen-digit card number space-padded to its declared X(16) width, because a COBOL PIC X field is left justified and space filled and those two trailing spaces are part of the field's value rather than absent from it. Both rows are pinned field by field as well as whole, so three things are asserted that no shipped fixture row can assert: that the numeric spans keep their leading zeros instead of being rendered as integers, that XREF-ACCT-ID's eleven digits survive a range an int cannot hold, and that XREF-CARD-NUM is read untrimmed. Everything around those values is the clean ladder: app/jcl/READXREF.jcl STEP05 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBACT03C with no PARM over the one XREFFILE DD, so no job parameter is declared; the OPEN at app/cbl/CBACT03C.cbl:120 succeeds, each row is displayed twice because CARD-XREF-RECORD is displayed at :96 inside 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT and again at :78 in the mainline loop, the third READ returns '10' and ends the loop, the CLOSE at :138 succeeds so :142 is never reached, and :85 emits the END banner with RETURN-CODE 0. No status is injected here: the abend ladder belongs to case06 through case13, where the CLOSE failing with '42' is case12 and with '96' is case13. The expected values are statically derived from app/cbl/CBACT03C.cbl, app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy, app/jcl/READXREF.jcl and the shipped rows of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt, never captured from a legacy execution (AAP risk R-A).
